program: pre-registration literature survey: which of the seven breakthrough directions (data axis, domain specialists, fixed code-geometry transforms, second-order pooling, scattering, shallow learned encoder, frontier-map framing) is ALREADY done in the literature? (13 Aug 2026)

registration_notes.N94.1: This is a SURVEY for the advisory breakthrough plan of 13 Aug 2026 - not a claim audit and NOT a novelty search. The hypothesis under test is that most of the seven directions are ALREADY established (they are named after classic pre-deep-learning image coding); the survey documents the displacing/presence evidence per direction, never an absence.
registration_notes.N94.2: Question registered before search: for each of the seven directions (D1 data-axis scaling of frozen codes, D2 per-domain specialists, D3 fixed nonlinear/spatial code geometry, D4 second-order/bilinear pooling, D5 scattering/fixed filter banks, D6 shallow learned patch encoder, D7 frontier-map framing), what is the nearest prior art that already does it, and which direction survives as an unmeasured object for this programme?
registration_notes.N94.3: Anchors are recall probes: each MUST be retrieved by a topic query that does NOT contain its title, else the search is insensitive and every 'not found' is worthless.
registration_notes.N94.4: Query families are phrased to find displacing work (work that already measures or builds the direction), not work that merely agrees in spirit.
registration_notes.N94.5: Empty queries are recorded, not dropped. Rate-limited queries are retried and residual failures recorded separately from genuinely empty results.
registration_notes.N94.6: Absence from these indexes is UNRESOLVED, never 'new' or 'first'. Unauthenticated public search cannot support a novelty claim.
registration_notes.N94.7: Title/abstract mark a source live; only primary text with a located passage may count as displacement.
registration_notes.N94.8: This evidence is a dated snapshot and is NOT replayable: the indexes change and the network is not a sealed corpus. The run records its date and the exact query strings so a reader can repeat the search, not so the bytes can be reproduced.
registration_notes.N94.9: Instrument reused from M127/M129/M132 (audit_v13_prior_art): arXiv two-stage AND-then-OR, Semantic Scholar with retry; S2 rate-limiting recorded as failures, not empty.
registration_notes.N94.10: Recall probes pair a paper whose existence is not in doubt with a topic query that omits its title. A probe that fails means the family it covers cannot be searched for absence; the positive-control probes must ALL be retrieved or the run is broken rather than informative.
registration_notes.N94.11: Local query-result cache (registered 13 Aug 2026, added AFTER the first live run of this config but BEFORE the cached re-run): successful results are stored in data/litsearch_cache.json keyed by (source, max_results, query) with fetched_at/origin provenance; a cached record is a dated snapshot and is marked from_cache in the evidence. Failures (HTTP 429) are never cached. Seed sources: m87/m88/m127/m129/m132/m135 evidence files.
registration_notes.N94.12: The first live run (evidence logs/results/v16/m135_breakthrough_prior_art_litsearch/evidence.json) used this config WITHOUT the cache notes and WITH live fetches; its config hash reflects that state. The cached re-run (logs/results/v16/m135_breakthrough_prior_art_litsearch_cached) is a cache-only validation: zero network calls; any query missing from the cache is recorded as a failure. Both are dated snapshots and neither is replayable.

D1.statement: Scaling the DATA axis for fixed/frozen (untrained) feature codes is already studied: accuracy-vs-training-set-size curves for non-learned encoders, and the frozen-construction vs trained-backbone data-scaling comparison.
queries: random feature classifier more training data accuracy
frozen feature extractor linear probe dataset size
kernel ridge regression large dataset scaling
ridge classifier data size random projection

D2.statement: Per-domain / per-group specialists routed by domain already exist: multi-domain networks with domain-specific branches, residual adapters, MoE-style routing over specialists.
queries: domain adaptation residual adapters per domain
mixture of experts domain routing classification

D3.statement: Fixed nonlinear/spatial code geometry is already the standard pre-deep image code: Fisher vectors, VLAD, power/signed-square-root normalization, spatial pyramids, multi-scale patches.
queries: signed square root power normalization descriptor

D4.statement: Second-order / covariance / bilinear pooling with closed-form or linear heads is already established.

D5.statement: Fixed filter-bank / scattering transforms (non-learned deep features) as classifiers are already established, including learned-scattering hybrids.
queries: fixed filter bank convolutional features classification

D6.statement: A shallow single-layer learned patch encoder / filter bank trained without backprop through a trunk already exists: dictionary learning, conv kernel networks, unsupervised patch feature learning.

D7.statement: The frontier-map framing - comparing fixed/random constructions against trained backbones at matched cost, the 'price of learning' - is already measured.
queries: random features versus deep networks comparison
fixed features versus learned features accuracy
